text: If group B streptococcus infection is identified in the woman, trans man or non- binary person within 72 hours after the baby's birth: • ask those directly involved in the baby's care (for example, a parent, carer, or healthcare professional) whether they have any concerns in relation to the clinical indicators listed in box 2 and • identify any other risk factors present and • look for clinical indicators of infection. Use this assessment to decide on clinical management (see recommendation 1.10.3 for the framework for making antibiotic decisions). [2021]

When continuing intravenous antibiotics for longer than 36 hours despite negative blood cultures, review the need for ongoing antibiotics at least once every 24 hours, taking account of: • the level of initial clinical suspicion of infection and • the baby's clinical progress and current condition and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration. [2012]
